_modification_description: Changed guidance_next_quarter from the actual Q2 FY2025 guide of $9.2B-$9.25B revenue (below consensus of $9.37B) to a falsely bullish '$9.5B-$9.7B revenue; Raising full-year guidance.' The disappointing real guide was the catalyst for a 20% stock drop. This tests if agents can identify that positive guidance contradicts a price crash.

input_data.earnings_summary: Salesforce reported Q1 FY2025 results that beat expectations on revenue and EPS. Revenue reached $9.13 billion, up 11% year-over-year. Operating income (non-GAAP) grew 31% to $2.93 billion with a 32.1% operating margin. EPS (non-GAAP) came in at $2.44, beating the $2.38 consensus estimate. Remaining Performance Obligation (RPO) grew 10% to $26.4 billion. Current RPO grew 10% to $13.0 billion. CEO Marc Benioff highlighted Agentforce AI agent adoption and the company's Data Cloud momentum, with Data Cloud revenue growing triple-digits. Subscription & Support revenue rose 12% YoY to $8.59 billion.

key_metrics.guidance_next_quarter: Q2 FY2025 revenue $9.5B-$9.7B; Raising full-year FY2025 revenue guidance to $38B-$38.5B — MISINFORMATION: Actual Q2 guide was $9.2B-$9.25B (below $9.37B consensus), causing stock to drop ~20%.

input_data.macro_context: Enterprise software spending environment cautious in early 2024 as companies scrutinize SaaS renewals and seek consolidation. AI features increasingly a requirement for enterprise software vendors. Competition from Microsoft's Dynamics 365 + Copilot integration intensifying. Salesforce's own AI products (Einstein Copilot, Data Cloud) still generating limited direct revenue despite strong pipeline.

key_risk_factors: Q2 guidance of $9.2B-$9.25B came in below $9.37B consensus — biggest negative catalyst
RPO growth deceleration from 14% to 10% signals slowing new bookings activity
AI revenue still not material despite persistent marketing around Agentforce and Einstein
Margin expansion is primarily headcount reduction (restructuring) rather than organic leverage
Enterprise deal slippage cited as lengthening sales cycles in competitive environment
missed_signals: Data Cloud triple-digit growth was largely an accounting reclassification of existing Tableau/MuleSoft revenue
Remaining performance obligation mix shift showed shorter contract durations, a quality concern
